+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""OCR with Occular-OCR (DBNet + SVTR + Russian n-gram beam LM).
+
+Russian-first document OCR, ONNX Runtime on CPU. Raw verbatim output.
+
+Usage:
+  python occular_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out.txt> [n_pages]
+"""
+import glob
+import os
+import sys
+import time
+
+from occular import OCRPipeline, Settings
+
+PAGES = sys.argv[1]
+OUT = sys.argv[2]
+N = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 63
+DEVICE = os.environ.get("OCCULAR_DEVICE", "cpu")
+
+pipe = OCRPipeline(Settings(gpu=(DEVICE == "cuda"), lm=True))
+
+pages = sorted(
+    p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(PAGES, "*"))
+    if p.lower().endswith((".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"))
+)[:N]
+out = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8")
+for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
+    t0 = time.time()
+    try:
+        lines = [ln.get("text", "") for ln in pipe.process_image(p) if ln.get("text")]
+        txt = "\n".join(lines)
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+        txt = f"<ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}>"
+    dt = time.time() - t0
+    print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {os.path.basename(p)} {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
+    out.write(f"===== {os.path.basename(p)} ({dt:.1f}s) =====\n{txt}\n\n")
+    out.flush()
+out.close()
+print("[i] done", flush=True)

# manga-ocr

Сырой (verbatim) OCR русскоязычной главы манхвы разными движками, плюс скрипты
и workflow, которыми это получено. Никакой коррекции и «додумывания» — только
то, что реально вернул движок.

Фикстура: `Том 1 Глава 74` (63 страницы JPG, внутри `fixtures/vol1-ch74.cbz`).

## Что внутри

- `scripts/normcap_ocr.py` — ансамбль через OCR-слой NormCap (Tesseract):
  конфиги `resize_factor × psm`, победа по средней уверенности. Основной движок.
- `scripts/easyocr_ocr.py` — EasyOCR.
- `scripts/florence_ocr.py` — крошечный VLM `microsoft/Florence-2-base-ft` (463 МБ) с задачей `<OCR>`.
- `scripts/mobile_vlm_ocr.py` — маленькие VLM (`SmolVLM-256M-Instruct` 513 МБ и др.).
- `.github/workflows/ocr-win.yml` — прогон NormCap/EasyOCR на Windows-раннере.
- `results/*.txt` — полученные сырые транскрипты.

## Результаты (63 страницы)

| Движок | Размер | Скорость | Качество на этом тексте |
|---|---|---|---|
| NormCap / Tesseract-`rus` | ~15 МБ (tessdata) | ~9 с/стр | **лучший**, читаемый русский текст |
| EasyOCR | ~100 МБ | ~30–90 с/стр | плохо: системно `Л→/`, `Н→H`, `Д→А/4`, `Ж→AI` |
| Florence-2-base-ft (VLM) | 463 МБ | ~170–200 с/стр (CPU) | частично: кириллицу узнаёт, но с ошибками и клеит строки без пробелов |
| SmolVLM-256M-Instruct (VLM) | 513 МБ | ~10–250 с/стр (CPU) | не OCR: описывает картинку, галлюцинирует |

Вывод: среди моделей ≤600 МБ Florence-2-base-ft — единственная, что реально
читает текст, но по точности уступает Tesseract/NormCap; SmolVLM-256M для OCR
непригодна.

```bash
# NormCap (нужен tesseract с языком rus)
python scripts/normcap_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out_dir>

# EasyOCR
python scripts/easyocr_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out_dir>

# Florence-2 (transformers, trust_remote_code; CPU ок)
pip install torch transformers timm
python scripts/florence_ocr.py microsoft/Florence-2-base-ft <pages_dir> <out.txt> 63

# SmolVLM-256M
pip install torch transformers accelerate einops
python scripts/mobile_vlm_ocr.py HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct <pages_dir> <out.txt> 63
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""OCR with PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 East-Slavic mobile recognizer."""
import glob
import os
import sys
import time

import os as _os
_os.environ.setdefault('FLAGS_use_mkldnn','0')
from paddleocr import PaddleOCR

PAGES = sys.argv[1]
OUT = sys.argv[2]
N = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 5
MODEL = os.environ.get("ESLAV_MODEL", "eslav_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec")

ocr = PaddleOCR(
    text_recognition_model_name=MODEL,
    use_doc_orientation_classify=False,
    use_doc_unwarping=False,
    use_textline_orientation=True,
    device="cpu",
    enable_mkldnn=False,
)

pages = sorted(
    p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(PAGES, "*"))
    if p.lower().endswith((".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"))
)[:N]
out = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8")
for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
    t0 = time.time()
    lines = []
    try:
        for r in ocr.predict(p):
            lines.extend(r["rec_texts"])
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        lines = [f"<ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}>"]
    dt = time.time() - t0
    print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {os.path.basename(p)} {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
    out.write(f"===== {os.path.basename(p)} ({dt:.1f}s) =====\n")
    out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n\n")
    out.flush()
out.close()
print("[i] done", flush=True)

10: page, the config with the highest mean word confidence. Output is verbatim OCR —
11: no correction, no invented words.
12: 
13: Usage:
14:   python normcap_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out_dir> [--tess-cmd PATH] [--tessdata DIR]
15: """

display.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""NormCap-based OCR over a folder of manga page images.

Uses NormCap's own detection layer (normcap.detection.ocr) as a library:
  - NormCap's enhance.preprocess() for upscaling (resize_factor)
  - NormCap's tesseract wrapper (perform_ocr -> TSV word/line metadata)
  - NormCap's OcrResult.add_linebreaks() for raw text reconstruction

Runs an ensemble of (resize_factor, psm) configs per page and keeps, for every
page, the config with the highest mean word confidence. Output is verbatim OCR —
no correction, no invented words.

Usage:
  python normcap_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out_dir> [--tess-cmd PATH] [--tessdata DIR]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

os.environ.setdefault("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "offscreen")

from PySide6.QtGui import QGuiApplication, QImage  # noqa: E402

from normcap.detection.ocr import tesseract  # noqa: E402
from normcap.detection.ocr.enhance import preprocess  # noqa: E402
from normcap.detection.ocr.models import OEM, PSM, OcrResult, TessArgs  # noqa: E402

# (name, resize_factor, psm, lang)
CONFIGS = [
    ("r2_psm3", 2.0, PSM.AUTO, "rus"),
    ("r3_psm3", 3.0, PSM.AUTO, "rus"),
    ("r4_psm3", 4.0, PSM.AUTO, "rus"),
    ("r3_psm6", 3.0, PSM.SINGLE_BLOCK, "rus"),
    ("r3_psm11", 3.0, PSM.SPARSE_TEXT, "rus"),
    ("r3_psm12", 3.0, PSM.SPARSE_TEXT_OSD, "rus"),
]
IMG_EXT = (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp", ".bmp")


def find_tesseract(explicit: str | None) -> str:
    if explicit and Path(explicit).exists():
        return explicit
    if env := os.environ.get("TESSERACT_CMD"):
        return env
    if found := shutil.which("tesseract"):
        return found
    candidates = [
        r"C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR\tesseract.exe",
        r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Tesseract-OCR\tesseract.exe",
        "/usr/bin/tesseract",
        "/usr/local/bin/tesseract",
    ]
    for c in candidates:
        if Path(c).exists():
            return c
    raise FileNotFoundError("tesseract binary not found")


def _download(url: str, target: Path) -> None:
    import urllib.request

    print(f"[i] downloading {url}", flush=True)
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, target)


def ensure_lang(tess_cmd: str, tessdata: str | None, lang: str) -> str | None:
    """Make sure `lang` (+ osd) traineddata is available; return tessdata dir."""
    langs: list[str] = []
    try:
        langs = tesseract.get_languages(tess_cmd, tessdata)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"[w] --list-langs failed: {exc}", flush=True)
    if lang in langs:
        print(f"[i] '{lang}' already available in tesseract default tessdata", flush=True)
        return tessdata
    # Tesseract can't find the language: drop traineddata into a local dir and
    # point Tesseract at it via --tessdata-dir. `osd` is needed by psm 12.
    local = Path(tessdata) if tessdata else Path.cwd() / "tessdata"
    local.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for code in (lang, "osd"):
        target = local / f"{code}.traineddata"
        if not target.exists():
            url = f"https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata_fast/raw/main/{code}.traineddata"
            try:
                _download(url, target)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                print(f"[w] could not download {code}: {exc}", flush=True)
    return str(local)


def ocr_page(img_path: str, tess_cmd: str, tessdata: str | None) -> tuple[str, str, tuple]:
    img = QImage(img_path)
    if img.isNull():
        print(f"[w] {img_path}: QImage failed to load", flush=True)
        return "NONE", "", (0, 0.0, 0)
    best = None
    for name, rz, psm, lang in CONFIGS:
        try:
            im = preprocess(img, resize_factor=rz, padding=0)
            args = TessArgs(tessdata, lang, OEM.DEFAULT, psm).as_list()
            words = tesseract.perform_ocr(tesseract_bin_path=tess_cmd, image=im, args=args)
            res = OcrResult(None, words, im)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"[w] {img_path} {name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", flush=True)
            continue
        good = [w for w in res.words if w.get("conf", 0) >= 50 and len(w["text"].strip()) >= 2]
        # Rank by confidence first: sparse PSMs (11/12) win on word count but
        # drag in art noise. Among configs with a near-equal mean confidence,
        # prefer the one that read more real words.
        score = (round(res.mean_conf, 1), len(good), res.num_chars)
        if best is None or score > best[2]:
            best = (name, res.text, score)
    if best is None:
        return "NONE", "", (0, 0.0, 0)
    return best[0], best[1], best[2]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("pages_dir")
    ap.add_argument("out_dir")
    ap.add_argument("--tess-cmd", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--tessdata", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    app = QGuiApplication.instance() or QGuiApplication(sys.argv)

    tess_cmd = find_tesseract(args.tess_cmd)
    tessdata = ensure_lang(tess_cmd, args.tessdata, "rus")
    print(f"[i] tesseract: {tess_cmd}", flush=True)
    print(f"[i] tessdata : {tessdata}", flush=True)

    pages = sorted(
        p
        for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(args.pages_dir, "*"))
        if p.lower().endswith(IMG_EXT)
    )
    print(f"[i] pages    : {len(pages)}", flush=True)

    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    txt = (out / "transcript.txt").open("w", encoding="utf-8")
    log = (out / "config_log.tsv").open("w", encoding="utf-8")
    result = {}

    for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
        name, text, score = ocr_page(p, tess_cmd, tessdata)
        base = os.path.basename(p)
        txt.write(f"===== {base} =====\n{text}\n\n")
        txt.flush()
        log.write(f"{base}\t{name}\t{score}\n")
        log.flush()
        result[base] = {"config": name, "score": list(score), "text": text}
        print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {base}: {name} {score}", flush=True)

    txt.close()
    log.close()
    (out / "result.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    print("[i] done", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""EasyOCR over a folder of page images (for comparison with NormCap).

Usage:
  python easyocr_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out_dir>
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

IMG_EXT = (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp", ".bmp")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("pages_dir")
    ap.add_argument("out_dir")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    import easyocr  # imported late so the step can be skipped cheaply

    reader = easyocr.Reader(["ru", "en"], gpu=False, verbose=False)

    pages = sorted(
        p
        for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(args.pages_dir, "*"))
        if p.lower().endswith(IMG_EXT)
    )
    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    txt = (out / "transcript.txt").open("w", encoding="utf-8")
    result = {}

    for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
        base = os.path.basename(p)
        lines = reader.readtext(p, detail=0, paragraph=False)
        text = "\n".join(lines)
        txt.write(f"===== {base} =====\n{text}\n\n")
        txt.flush()
        result[base] = text
        print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {base}: {len(lines)} lines", flush=True)

    txt.close()
    (out / "result.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    print("[i] done", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

on:

          python -c "import zipfile,sys; zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" $cbz $pages
          $n = (Get-ChildItem $pages -File).Count

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tiny (<600MB) VLM OCR: Florence-2-base-ft with the <OCR> task prompt."""
import glob
import os
import sys
import time

import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor

MODEL = sys.argv[1]
PAGES = sys.argv[2]
OUT = sys.argv[3]
N = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 5
TASK = "<OCR>"

print(f"[i] loading {MODEL}", flush=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    MODEL, trust_remote_code=True, torch_dtype=torch.float16
)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL, trust_remote_code=True)
model.eval()

pages = sorted(
    p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(PAGES, "*"))
    if p.lower().endswith((".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"))
)[:N]
out = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8")
for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
    img = Image.open(p).convert("RGB")
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        inputs = processor(text=TASK, images=img, return_tensors="pt")
        with torch.inference_mode():
            ids = model.generate(
                input_ids=inputs["input_ids"],
                pixel_values=inputs["pixel_values"].to(torch.float16),
                max_new_tokens=1024,
                num_beams=3,
                do_sample=False,
            )
        raw = processor.batch_decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False)[0]
        parsed = processor.post_process_generation(
            raw, task=TASK, image_size=(img.width, img.height)
        )
        txt = parsed.get(TASK, raw)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        txt = f"<ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}>"
    dt = time.time() - t0
    print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {os.path.basename(p)} {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
    out.write(f"===== {os.path.basename(p)} ({dt:.1f}s) =====\n{txt}\n\n")
    out.flush()
out.close()
print("[i] done", flush=True)

display.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""OCR manga pages with a small "mobile" VLM (SmolVLM / moondream2).

Raw, verbatim prompt: read every visible text, no translation, no invention.

Usage:
  python mobile_vlm_ocr.py <model_id[@revision]> <pages_dir> <out.txt> [n_pages]
"""
import glob
import os
import sys
import time

import torch
from PIL import Image

MODEL = sys.argv[1]
REVISION = None
if "@" in MODEL:
    MODEL, REVISION = MODEL.split("@", 1)
PAGES = sys.argv[2]
OUT = sys.argv[3]
N = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 5

PROMPT = (
    "Read ALL text on this manga page exactly as written. "
    "Output only the text, line by line, in the original language. "
    "Do not translate, do not describe the picture, do not explain."
)

IS_MOONDREAM = "moondream" in MODEL.lower()

print(f"[i] loading {MODEL} rev={REVISION}", flush=True)
if IS_MOONDREAM:
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        MODEL, trust_remote_code=True, revision=REVISION, torch_dtype=torch.float16
    )
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL, revision=REVISION)
else:
    from transformers import AutoModelForVision2Seq, AutoProcessor

    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL, revision=REVISION)
    ip = processor.image_processor
    if hasattr(ip, "size") and hasattr(ip, "max_image_size"):
        ip.size = dict(ip.max_image_size)
        ip.do_image_splitting = False
    model = AutoModelForVision2Seq.from_pretrained(
        MODEL, revision=REVISION, torch_dtype=torch.float16
    )
model.eval()


def run(img: Image.Image) -> str:
    if IS_MOONDREAM:
        if hasattr(model, "query"):
            return model.query(img, PROMPT).strip()
        enc = model.encode_image(img)
        return model.answer_question(enc, PROMPT, tok).strip()
    messages = [
        {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image"}, {"type": "text", "text": PROMPT}]}
    ]
    text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True)
    inputs = processor(text=text, images=[img], return_tensors="pt")
    with torch.inference_mode():
        ids = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False)
    gen = ids[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:]
    return processor.decode(gen, skip_special_tokens=True).strip()


pages = sorted(
    p
    for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(PAGES, "*"))
    if p.lower().endswith((".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"))
)[:N]
out = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8")
for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
    img = Image.open(p).convert("RGB")
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        txt = run(img)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        txt = f"<ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}>"
    dt = time.time() - t0
    print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {os.path.basename(p)} {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
    out.write(f"===== {os.path.basename(p)} ({dt:.1f}s) =====\n{txt}\n\n")
    out.flush()
out.close()
print("[i] done", flush=True)

kraken is a turn-key OCR system optimized for historical and non-Latin script material.
Features ¶
kraken’s main features are:
* Fully trainable layout analysis and character recognition
* Right-to-Left , BiDi , and Top-to-Bottom script support
* ALTO , PageXML, abbyXML, and hOCR output
* Word bounding boxes and character cuts
* Multi-script recognition support
* Public repository of model files
* Lightweight model files
* Variable recognition network architectures
Installation ¶
Kraken can be run on Linux or Mac OS X (both x64 and ARM). Installation through the on-board pip utility and the anaconda scientific computing python are supported.
Installation using Pip ¶
Finally you’ll have to scrounge up a recognition model to do the actual recognition of characters. To download the default English text recognition model and place it in the user’s kraken directory:
$ kraken get 10 .5281/zenodo.2577813
A list of libre models available in the central repository can be retrieved by running:
$ kraken list
A generalized model for English printed text
The structure of an OCR software consists of multiple steps, primarily preprocessing, segmentation, and recognition, each of which takes the output of the previous step and sometimes additional files such as models and templates that define how a particular transformation is to be performed.
In kraken these are separated into different subcommands that can be chained or ran separately:
Recognizing text on an image using the default parameters including the prerequisite step of page segmentation:
$ kraken -i image.tif image.txt segment -bl ocr
Loading RNN     ✓
Processing      ⣻
To segment an image into reading-order sorted baselines and regions:
$ kraken -i bw.tif lines.json segment -bl
To OCR an image using the default model:
$ kraken -i bw.tif image.txt segment -bl ocr
To OCR an image using the default model and serialize the output using the ALTO template:
$ kraken -a -i bw.tif image.txt segment -bl ocr

Historical Russian TrOCR Model for Civil Script (ru-trocr-1700s)
Model Description
This model is specifically trained to recognize Russian Civil Script (гражданский шрифт) from the 18th century. It handles the following character sets:
* Historical letters: ѣ, і, ѳ, ѵ, ъ
* Civil script variations of standard Cyrillic characters
* Both uppercase and lowercase variants
* Special typographic features of 18th-century printing
Model Performance Metrics
* Character Error Rate (CER): 1.69%
* Word Error Rate (WER): 5.75%
* Sequence Accuracy: 80.21%
* Training Loss: 0.0403
* Evaluation Loss: 0.0351
Training Details
* Base Model: TrOCR
* Training Duration: ~25.5 hours
* Epochs: 3
* Steps: 1227
* Training Samples per Second: 0.428
* Special Focus: Civil script character recognition including historical letters and their variants
* Training Data: 18th-century Russian books from the National Library of Russia
Historical Context
The model is trained on texts printed in Civil Script (гражданский шрифт), introduced by Peter the Great's reform in 1708. This script represents a significant transition in Russian typography from Church Slavonic to a more modernized form of writing.
Limitations and Recommendations
* Optimized for line-level recognition of historical Russian texts in Civil Script
* Best performance on well-segmented lines
* May require pre-processing for damaged or low-quality images
* Specifically tuned for 18th-century Russian printing conventions
Usage Example

Let me structure the answer well. Key additional engines:

Already in repo:
- NormCap/Tesseract rus
- EasyOCR ru
- Florence-2-base-ft
- SmolVLM-256M
- PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 eslav mobile rec

New candidates, specialized for Russian/Cyrillic:
1. **Occular-OCR** (Bodhi42/Occular-ocr) — DBNet + SVTR + beam + Russian n-gram LM. Russian-specific, claims ~35% fewer word errors. Very relevant. Check pip availability. Might be recent 2026.
2. **PP-OCRv5 server rec** with `cyrillic_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec` and `latin`/`eslav` variants; also `cyrillic_PP-OCRv3_mobile_rec` (legacy, high acc on some datasets). Also PaddleOCR-VL (0.9B VLM, 109 langs incl Russian).
3. **Surya OCR 2** (650M, ru 88.8%) — strong.
4. **TrOCR Russian**: raxtemur/trocr-base-ru (printed/handwritten synth), kazars24/trocr-base-handwritten-ru, cyrillic-trocr/trocr-handwritten-cyrillic, taiga75/ru-trocr-1700s (historical). Line-level recognizer, needs detection (can combine with CRAFT/DBNet).
5. **Kraken** — historical/non-Latin, has Cyrillic models. Good for old prints.
6. **RapidOCR** — ONNX PaddleOCR, lightweight, supports cyrillic/eslav dicts. Fast on CPU.
7. **MMOCR** — has some Cyrillic support via recog models; less turnkey.
8. **docTR** — multilingual, weaker on Russian.
9. **GOT-OCR2.0** (580M VLM), **Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B**, **InternVL2.5-1B/2B**, **MiniCPM-V**, **dots.ocr**, **DeepSeek-OCR**, **LightOnOCR-2-1B**, **Chandra OCR 2** — general VLMs good at Russian.
10. **Tesseract with tessdata_best + rus+eng**, and **Tesseract 5 LSTM**, plus different PSM; also `osd`. NormCap already uses fast? Actually it downloads tessdata_fast. Switching to tessdata_best could improve.
11. **Yandex Vision OCR** — best-in-class Russian but cloud/paid (not offline).
12. **PaddleOCR-VL** / **PP-StructureV3** for document parsing.
13. **RoseTTA / Cuneiform** — obsolete.
14. **Cloud: Google Vision, Azure, AWS Textract** support Russian.

Also specialized Russian:
- **Sber / Salute** models? not open.
- **"ru-ocr" models on HF**: "nastyboget/..." datasets, "Py". TrOCR ru.
- **"Locate Anything"** etc.

Given CPU-only and the repo's focus on ≤600MB, the top realistic additions are: PaddleOCR cyrillic/variants, RapidOCR, Surya OCR 2 (650M), TrOCR-ru (needs detector), Occular-OCR, Kraken, and bigger VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-3B, GOT-OCR).

# Occular-OCR

[](#occular-ocr)

**State-of-the-art OCR for Russian documents — with a zero-compilation install.**

[![Code License: Apache 2.0](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/00f16d398167623ebcd90d456fa0ae85c0dd566a5ee0c5d6fb2fe4e4bc00ed32/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f436f64652d417061636865253230322e302d3266356666302e737667)](/Bodhi42/Occular-ocr/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Weights: OpenRAIL-M](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/cb041d4dd7c4c0d8e284855ffe16f8e4438a20478b2e1e2781788ff09da18379/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f576569676874732d4149253230507562732532304f70656e5241494c2d2d4d2d6530353333612e737667)](/Bodhi42/Occular-ocr/blob/main/WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md) [![Python 3.8+](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/fe4ef095b72430b9538c90222b5018a530d7cef901760474c5a5edd7ce231506/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f707974686f6e2d332e382532422d3136313831642e737667)](#installation) [![pip install — no compiler](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/cb1df31bfc0a719ef5164e3ae2381eaf02a4bb16ff3225bfd41b84e6805d4502/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f696e7374616c6c2d707572652532307069702532302543322542372532306e6f253230636f6d70696c65722d3066396435382e737667)](#installation)

🇬🇧 **English**  ·  [🇷🇺 Русский](#russian)

Occular-OCR is a document OCR library purpose-built for **Russian**. It pairs a DBNet text detector with an SVTR recognizer and a beam-search decoder guided by a Russian language model — and reads Russian documents **markedly better than existing open-source OCR**, especially the hard stuff: forms, certificates, bank statements, IDs, receipts.

It installs with a single `pip install` on Windows, Linux and macOS — **no C/C++ toolchain, no CUDA, nothing to build.**

## Why Occular-OCR

[](#why-occular-ocr)

Occular-OCR is built for Russian and reads it dramatically better than existing open-source OCR: **~35 % fewer word errors than the next-best open-source engine** in an end-to-end benchmark, and ranking **#1** against large vision-language models and other leading OCR engines on a page-level document benchmark. The gap is widest exactly where general-purpose OCR struggles: dense forms, certificates, invoices and IDs.

 ![opendocs page-level benchmark — Occular-OCR ranks #1 by character error rate against large vision-language models, Yandex Vision, Surya, Tesseract, RapidOCR and others](/Bodhi42/Occular-ocr/raw/main/assets/benchmark_opendocs.png)

Character error rate (per-page mean, capped) on **113 real Russian document pages**, scored against an independent, per-page ground truth built with Fable. Lower is better.

The pages are a cross-section of everyday Russian paperwork — powers of attorney, bank statements, invoices and VAT invoices, passports and IDs, contracts, certificates, applications and receipts. Because every page is a genuine document carrying private individuals' personal data, **the benchmark itself is not published.** That is also exactly why it matters: these are real, in-the-wild production documents, so the numbers reflect how OCR actually behaves on live document workloads far better than any synthetic or public dataset can.

-   **Russian-first accuracy.** Trained and tuned on Russian document data. Where other engines guess, Occular-OCR reads.
-   **Beam + language model, on by default.** A Russian n-gram language model cuts word errors ~18–25 % over plain greedy decoding — with **no model retraining**, just better decoding.
-   **Fast by default.** The default recognizer (`svtr_lcnet`) reads a dense page about **5× faster** on CPU than the previous one while keeping 99.6 % of its accuracy. The larger model is still one argument away: `recognizer="svtr_t"`.
-   **Handles sideways pages.** Turn on `orientation=True` and Occular detects a 0/90/180/270° rotation and straightens the page before reading it — for phone photos and bulk scans that come in rotated. Off by default; it only rotates when it is confident.
-   **Installs anywhere, no compiler.** The decoder is pure Python end to end, so you get top-tier decoding quality with **zero native dependencies**.
-   **CPU-first, GPU-ready.** Every model is ONNX and runs on CPU out of the box; set `gpu=True` to run the same models on CUDA through ONNX Runtime — no PyTorch.
-   **Batteries included.** Images and PDF, folder → `.txt`, reading order, automatic deskew.

---

## Installation

[](#installation)

pip install occular-ocr

That's it. No build tools, no CUDA. Model weights download automatically on first use and are cached locally. Requires a platform with ONNX Runtime wheels: Linux and Windows (x86\_64), Linux aarch64 and macOS — except Intel Macs on Python 3.14, where ONNX Runtime has no build yet (use Python ≤ 3.13).

### GPU (optional)

[](#gpu-optional)

Every model is ONNX; on GPU the same files run on CUDA through ONNX Runtime, so there are no extra weights and no PyTorch. On Linux and Windows the base install already uses the GPU build of ONNX Runtime (it runs on CPU just as fast when there is no GPU). The extra only adds the CUDA and cuDNN libraries from pip, so you need nothing but an NVIDIA driver:

pip install "occular-ocr\[gpu\]"    # CUDA + cuDNN from pip; no system CUDA needed

Then pass `gpu=True` (see below). If CUDA can't be loaded, Occular says why once and runs on CPU. TF32 is disabled on GPU, so the text matches the CPU path.

from occular import ocr

text \= ocr("document.png")        \# an image, or a "scan.pdf"

from occular import ocr\_detailed

for line in ocr\_detailed("document.png"):

## Configuration

[](#configuration)

All behaviour is controlled by `Settings` (or the equivalent keyword arguments on `ocr`). Print the current defaults at any time:

from occular import Settings
print(Settings())

Setting

Default

What it does

`num_threads`

`None`

CPU threads for inference. `None` → `min(cores, 4)`.

`gpu`

`False`

Run on **GPU (CUDA via ONNX Runtime)**. CUDA libraries: `occular-ocr[gpu]`; falls back to CPU if unavailable.

`orientation`

`False`

Detect a 0/90/180/270° page rotation and straighten it before detection — for phone photos and bulk scans that arrive sideways. Applied only when the model is at least 0.8 confident.

`deskew`

`True`

Auto-correct skewed scans (a few degrees) before detection.

`unwarp`

`None`

Neural dewarping (UVDoc) for curved or photographed pages. `None` → off. A Hugging Face model id or local folder with `model.onnx` (e.g. `"Shivin11/occular-uvdoc"`), or a ready `UVDocUnwarper`. Runs on ONNX, no extra dependencies.

`unwarp_gate`

`True`

How to decide whether to apply the dewarp (when `unwarp` is set). `True` → readability self-gate: apply only if it improves text readability by at least `unwarp_margin`×. `False`/`None` → always apply. A number → use it as the readability threshold. A callable `(res_orig, res_dewarped) -> bool` → your own rule.

`unwarp_margin`

`1.05`

Readability multiplier for the default gate (`unwarp_gate=True`). Higher → dewarp fires less often, but only when it clearly helps.

`lm`

`True`

Beam search + language model (best quality). `False` → fast greedy decoding, skips the LM download.

`reading_order`

`False`

Order lines for multi-column layouts. Needs an optional model: call `download_reading_order()` once first (see [below](#optional-reading-order-for-multi-column-pages)).

`languages`

`None`

Text language(s). `None` → Russian/English. A list of codes (e.g. `["uk"]`) or `"auto"` enables the multilingual model (12 more Cyrillic-script languages). See [Languages](#languages).

`detector`

`None`

Explicit detector name. `None` → default.

`recognizer`

`None`

Recognizer architecture: `"svtr_lcnet"` (default — light, ~5× faster on CPU) or `"svtr_t"` (the larger model). Both run on CPU and GPU.

### Full pipeline with every setting

[](#full-pipeline-with-every-setting)

from occular import OCRPipeline, Settings

pipe \= OCRPipeline(Settings(
    num\_threads\=8,        \# CPU threads (None -> min(cores, 4))
    gpu\=False,            \# True -> CUDA via ONNX Runtime (CUDA libs: occular-ocr\[gpu\])
    orientation\=False,    \# detect 0/90/180/270 rotation and straighten the page
    deskew\=True,          \# auto-correct skewed scans
    unwarp\=None,          \# UVDoc dewarp for curved/photo pages: "Shivin11/occular-uvdoc" or a local folder with model.onnx
    unwarp\_gate\=True,     \# True -> apply only if it improves readability (x unwarp\_margin); False -> always; number -> custom threshold; callable -> your rule
    unwarp\_margin\=1.05,   \# readability multiplier for the default unwarp gate
    lm\=True,              \# beam + language model; False -> greedy (faster, no LM download)
    reading\_order\=False,  \# multi-column reading order (optional model, see below)
    detector\=None,        \# None = default detector
    recognizer\=None,      \# None = svtr\_lcnet; "svtr\_t" = the larger model
))

result \= pipe.process\_image("document.png")
\# -> \[{"quad": \[\[x, y\], ...\], "text": "...", "confidence": 0.97}, ...\]

### One-liners

[](#one-liners)

from occular import ocr

ocr("document.png")                 \# CPU (default), full quality
ocr("document.png", gpu\=True)       \# GPU: CUDA via ONNX Runtime (CUDA libs: occular-ocr\[gpu\])

### Languages

[](#languages)

By default Occular reads **Russian and English**. Pass `languages=` to switch on the multilingual model, which adds **12 more Cyrillic-script languages**: Bashkir (`ba`), Belarusian (`be`), Bulgarian (`bg`), Chuvash (`cv`), Kazakh (`kk`), Kyrgyz (`ky`), Macedonian (`mk`), Mongolian (`mn`), Serbian (`sr`), Tajik (`tg`), Tatar (`tt`), Ukrainian (`uk`).

from occular import ocr

ocr("doc\_uk.png", languages\=\["uk"\])          \# a single language — fastest
ocr("mixed.png",  languages\=\["ru", "kk"\])    \# several — language is detected per line
ocr("scan.png",   languages\="auto")          \# auto-detect across all supported languages

ocr doc\_uk.png --languages uk                # or --lang uk
ocr mixed.png  --languages ru,kk
ocr scan.png   --languages auto

The right language weights download from the Hub on first use (only the ones you ask for). More languages are added over time in minor releases.

## Tables

[](#tables)

`TableRecognizer` finds tables on a page and reconstructs their structure — the row/column grid plus merged cells (`colspan`/`rowspan`):

import cv2
from occular import TableRecognizer

tr \= TableRecognizer()
page \= cv2.imread("report.png")
for t in tr(page):
    x0, y0, x1, y1, conf \= t\["bbox"\]
    print(f"table at {(x0, y0, x1, y1)}: {len(t\['rows'\])} rows × {len(t\['cols'\])} cols, "
          f"{len(t\['cells'\])} cells")

Detection, the row/column grid and merged cells all run on ONNX (CPU or `gpu=True`), with no extra dependencies.

## Optional: native decoder (faster)

[](#optional-native-decoder-faster)

The decoding stack is pure Python by default. An optional Rust module, `occular-decode`, is a drop-in accelerator: **byte-identical output**, but 5–13× faster per line and 17–48× per page, with lower memory. Once installed it is picked up automatically (pure Python stays as the fallback). Build/install instructions are in [`native/README.md`](/Bodhi42/Occular-ocr/blob/main/native/README.md).

## How it works

[](#how-it-works)

```
image ─▶ deskew ─▶ DBNet detector ─▶ crops ─▶ SVTR recognizer ─▶ beam + n-gram LM ─▶ text
```

The recognizer is a compact SVTR + CTC model exported to ONNX; the decoder is a CTC prefix beam search guided by a 4-gram Russian language model. The entire decoding stack — language model and beam search alike — is **pure Python**, which is what keeps `pip install` friction-free on every platform.

## Почему Occular-OCR

[](#почему-occular-ocr)

Occular-OCR заточен под русский и читает его значительно лучше существующего open-source OCR: **~35 % меньше ошибок слов, чем ближайший open-source-движок** в сквозном бенчмарке, и **#1** против больших vision-language моделей и других ведущих OCR-движков на постраничном бенчмарке. Разрыв максимален там, где универсальный OCR буксует: плотные формы, справки, счета, удостоверения.

 ![Постраничный бенчмарк opendocs — Occular-OCR на 1-м месте по ошибке символов против больших vision-language моделей, Yandex Vision, Surya, Tesseract, RapidOCR и других](/Bodhi42/Occular-ocr/raw/main/assets/benchmark_opendocs.png)

Ошибка символов (средняя по страницам, с отсечкой) на **113 реальных страницах русских документов**, против независимой постраничной эталонной разметки, сделанной с помощью Fable. Меньше — лучше.

Страницы — срез повседневного российского документооборота: доверенности, банковские выписки, счета и счёта-фактуры, паспорта и удостоверения, договоры, свидетельства, заявления и чеки. Поскольку каждая страница — настоящий документ с персональными данными физлиц, **сам бенчмарк не публикуется.** В этом же и его ценность: это реальные боевые документы, поэтому цифры отражают работу OCR на живом документопотоке гораздо лучше, чем любой синтетический или публичный набор.

-   **Точность под русский.** Обучен и настроен на русских документах. Там, где другие движки гадают, Occular-OCR читает.
-   **Beam + языковая модель по умолчанию.** Русская n-gram языковая модель снижает ошибки слов на ~18–25 % относительно жадного декодирования — **без дообучения модели**, просто лучше декодирование.
-   **Быстрый по умолчанию.** Распознаватель по умолчанию (`svtr_lcnet`) читает плотную страницу примерно **в 5 раз быстрее** на CPU, чем прежний, сохраняя 99,6 % его точности. Крупная модель — одним аргументом: `recognizer="svtr_t"`.
-   **Справляется со страницами боком.** Включи `orientation=True` — Occular определит поворот 0/90/180/270° и выпрямит страницу перед чтением: для фото с телефона и массовых сканов, приходящих повёрнутыми. По умолчанию выключено; поворачивает, только когда уверен.
-   **Ставится где угодно, без компилятора.** Декодер целиком на чистом Python — топовое качество декода с **нулевыми нативными зависимостями**.
-   **Сначала CPU, GPU — по желанию.** Все модели — ONNX, работают на CPU из коробки; `gpu=True` исполняет те же модели на CUDA через ONNX Runtime — без PyTorch.
-   **Всё в комплекте.** Картинки и PDF, папка → `.txt`, порядок чтения, автоматическое выпрямление наклона.

## Установка

[](#установка)

pip install occular-ocr

И всё. Без сборочных инструментов, без CUDA. Веса моделей скачиваются автоматически при первом запуске и кэшируются. Нужна платформа, для которой есть сборки ONNX Runtime: Linux и Windows (x86\_64), Linux aarch64 и macOS — кроме Intel-маков на Python 3.14, где сборки ONNX Runtime пока нет (подойдёт Python ≤ 3.13).

### GPU (опционально)

[](#gpu-опционально)

Все модели — ONNX; на GPU те же файлы исполняются на CUDA через ONNX Runtime, без отдельных весов и без PyTorch. На Linux и Windows базовая установка уже ставит GPU-сборку ONNX Runtime (без видеокарты она работает на CPU с той же скоростью). Экстра добавляет только библиотеки CUDA и cuDNN из pip — нужен лишь драйвер NVIDIA:

pip install "occular-ocr\[gpu\]"    # CUDA + cuDNN из pip; системная CUDA не нужна

Затем передай `gpu=True` (см. ниже). Если CUDA не загрузилась, Occular один раз скажет почему и продолжит на CPU. TF32 на GPU выключен, поэтому текст совпадает с CPU-путём.

## Настройки

[](#настройки)

Всё поведение задаётся через `Settings` (или эквивалентные именованные аргументы `ocr`). Посмотреть текущие дефолты можно в любой момент:

from occular import Settings
print(Settings())

Настройка

По умолчанию

Что делает

`num_threads`

`None`

CPU-потоки для инференса. `None` → `min(ядра, 4)`.

`gpu`

`False`

Гонять на **GPU (CUDA через ONNX Runtime)**. Библиотеки CUDA — `occular-ocr[gpu]`; при отсутствии — откат на CPU.

`orientation`

`False`

Определять поворот страницы 0/90/180/270° и выпрямлять до детекции — для фото с телефона и массовых сканов, приходящих боком. Срабатывает только при уверенности модели ≥ 0.8.

`deskew`

`True`

Автовыпрямление наклонённых сканов (несколько градусов) перед детекцией.

`unwarp`

`None`

Нейро-расправление изгиба (UVDoc) для изогнутых или сфотографированных страниц. `None` → выкл. Строка — HF model id или локальная папка с `model.onnx` (напр. `"Shivin11/occular-uvdoc"`), либо готовый `UVDocUnwarper`. Работает на ONNX, без доп. зависимостей.

`unwarp_gate`

`True`

Чем решать, применять ли расправление (когда `unwarp` задан). `True` → гейт по читаемости: применять, только если текст стал читаемее минимум в `unwarp_margin`× раз. `False`/`None` → применять всегда. Число → использовать как порог читаемости. Callable `(res_orig, res_dewarped) -> bool` → свой критерий.

`unwarp_margin`

`1.05`

Порог-множитель читаемости для дефолтного гейта (`unwarp_gate=True`). Больше → расправление срабатывает реже, но только когда явно помогает.

`lm`

`True`

Beam + языковая модель (лучшее качество). `False` → быстрое жадное декодирование, без скачивания LM.

`reading_order`

`False`

Упорядочивание строк для многоколоночных макетов. Нужна опциональная модель: один раз вызови `download_reading_order()` (см. [ниже](#%D0%BE%D0%BF%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%BB%D1%8C%D0%BD%D0%BE-%D0%BF%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%8F%D0%B4%D0%BE%D0%BA-%D1%87%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%8F-%D0%B4%D0%BB%D1%8F-%D0%BC%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B%D1%85-%D1%81%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%86)).

`languages`

`None`

Язык(и) текста. `None` → русский/английский. Список кодов (напр. `["uk"]`) или `"auto"` включает многоязычную модель (ещё 12 языков на кириллице). См. [Языки](#%D1%8F%D0%B7%D1%8B%D0%BA%D0%B8).

`detector`

`None`

Явное имя детектора. `None` → по умолчанию.

`recognizer`

`None`

Архитектура распознавателя: `"svtr_lcnet"` (по умолчанию — лёгкая, ~5× быстрее на CPU) или `"svtr_t"` (крупная). Обе работают и на CPU, и на GPU.

### Пайплайн со всеми настройками

[](#пайплайн-со-всеми-настройками)

from occular import OCRPipeline, Settings

pipe \= OCRPipeline(Settings(
    num\_threads\=8,        \# CPU-потоки (None -> min(ядра, 4))
    gpu\=False,            \# True -> CUDA через ONNX Runtime (библиотеки CUDA: occular-ocr\[gpu\])
    orientation\=False,    \# определять поворот 0/90/180/270 и выпрямлять страницу
    deskew\=True,          \# автовыпрямление наклона
    unwarp\=None,          \# UVDoc-расправление изгиба: "Shivin11/occular-uvdoc" или локальная папка с model.onnx
    unwarp\_gate\=True,     \# True -> применять, только если стало читаемее (x unwarp\_margin); False -> всегда; число -> свой порог; callable -> свой критерий
    unwarp\_margin\=1.05,   \# порог-множитель читаемости для дефолтного гейта
    lm\=True,              \# beam + языковая модель; False -> жадное (быстрее, без скачивания LM)
    reading\_order\=False,  \# порядок чтения для многоколоночных (опц. модель, см. ниже)
    detector\=None,        \# None = детектор по умолчанию
    recognizer\=None,      \# None = svtr\_lcnet; "svtr\_t" = крупная модель
))

result \= pipe.process\_image("document.png")
\# -> \[{"quad": \[\[x, y\], ...\], "text": "...", "confidence": 0.97}, ...\]

pages \= pipe.process\_pdf(

    dpi\=300,          \# разрешение рендеринга сканов (по умолчанию 300)
    force\_ocr\=False,  \# True: OCR даже для PDF с текстовым слоем
    workers\=4,        \# параллельные страницы (None = авто min(ядра, 4); 1 = последовательно)
)

### Однострочники

[](#однострочники)

from occular import ocr

ocr("document.png")                 \# CPU (по умолчанию), полное качество
ocr("document.png", gpu\=True)       \# GPU: CUDA через ONNX Runtime (библиотеки CUDA: occular-ocr\[gpu\])

ocr("document.png", deskew\=False)   \# без выпрямления наклона

### Языки

[](#языки)

По умолчанию Occular читает **русский и английский**. Аргумент `languages=` включает многоязычную модель — ещё **12 языков на кириллице**: башкирский (`ba`), белорусский (`be`), болгарский (`bg`), чувашский (`cv`), казахский (`kk`), киргизский (`ky`), македонский (`mk`), монгольский (`mn`), сербский (`sr`), таджикский (`tg`), татарский (`tt`), украинский (`uk`).

from occular import ocr

ocr("doc\_uk.png", languages\=\["uk"\])          \# один язык — быстрее всего
ocr("mixed.png",  languages\=\["ru", "kk"\])    \# несколько — язык определяется построчно
ocr("scan.png",   languages\="auto")          \# авто-определение среди всех поддерживаемых

ocr doc\_uk.png --languages uk                # или --lang uk
ocr mixed.png  --languages ru,kk
ocr scan.png   --languages auto

Веса нужного языка скачиваются с Hub при первом обращении (только те, что запросили). Новые языки добавляются со временем в минорных релизах.

## Таблицы

[](#таблицы)

`TableRecognizer` находит таблицы на странице и восстанавливает их структуру — сетку строк/столбцов и объединённые ячейки (`colspan`/`rowspan`):

import cv2
from occular import TableRecognizer

tr \= TableRecognizer()
page \= cv2.imread("report.png")
for t in tr(page):
    x0, y0, x1, y1, conf \= t\["bbox"\]
    print(f"таблица {(x0, y0, x1, y1)}: строк {len(t\['rows'\])} × столбцов {len(t\['cols'\])}, "
          f"ячеек {len(t\['cells'\])}")

Детекция, сетка строк/столбцов и объединённые ячейки — всё на ONNX (CPU или `gpu=True`), без доп. зависимостей.

## Как это работает

## Специализированные под русский/кириллицу
- **occular-ocr** (`pip install occular-ocr`) — DBNet + SVTR + beam с русской 4-gram LM. ONNX, CPU-first, без компилятора; заявляют ~35% меньше ошибок слов, чем ближайший open-source. Прямой аналог, но русско-заточенный. Веса: open для <8 сотрудников/20 млн ₽, иначе платно.

import os
import click
import json
import time
from collections import defaultdict

from surya.inference import SuryaInferenceManager
from surya.logging import configure_logging, get_logger
from surya.recognition import RecognitionPredictor
from surya.scripts.config import CLILoader

configure_logging()
logger = get_logger()


@click.command(help="OCR text — full-page OCR (one VLM call per page).")
@CLILoader.common_options
def ocr_text_cli(input_path: str, **kwargs):
    # Full-page OCR is the default path: one VLM call per page returns layout
    # + content together. Pages whose full-page output fails to parse fall
    # back to layout + per-block OCR automatically (see RecognitionPredictor).
    loader = CLILoader(input_path, kwargs, highres=True)

    manager = SuryaInferenceManager()
    rec_predictor = RecognitionPredictor(manager)

    start = time.time()
    page_results = rec_predictor(loader.highres_images, full_page=True)

    if loader.debug:
        logger.debug(f"OCR took {time.time() - start:.2f} seconds")

    out_preds = defaultdict(list)
    for name, page in zip(loader.names, page_results):
        out_pred = page.model_dump()
        out_pred["page"] = len(out_preds[name]) + 1
        out_preds[name].append(out_pred)

    with open(
        os.path.join(loader.result_path, "results.json"), "w+", encoding="utf-8"
    ) as f:
        json.dump(out_preds, f, ensure_ascii=False)

    logger.info(f"Wrote results to {loader.result_path}")

import torch

from pydantic import computed_field
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings
from pathlib import Path
from platformdirs import user_cache_dir


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    # General
    TORCH_DEVICE: Optional[str] = None
    IMAGE_DPI: int = 96  # used for layout + text detection (coarse structure)
    IMAGE_DPI_HIGHRES: int = 192  # used for recognition + table rec (fine glyphs)
    IN_STREAMLIT: bool = False

    S3_BASE_URL: str = "https://models.datalab.to"
    PARALLEL_DOWNLOAD_WORKERS: int = 10
    MODEL_CACHE_DIR: str = str(Path(user_cache_dir("datalab")) / "models")
    LOGLEVEL: str = "INFO"

    RESULT_DIR: str = "results"
    BASE_DIR: str = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    FONT_DIR: str = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "static", "fonts")

    @computed_field
    def TORCH_DEVICE_MODEL(self) -> str:
        if self.TORCH_DEVICE is not None:
            return self.TORCH_DEVICE
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            return "cuda"
        if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
            return "mps"
        return "cpu"

    SURYA_GGUF_LOCAL_MMPROJ_PATH: Optional[str] = None

    SURYA_INFERENCE_URL: Optional[str] = None  # external server, skip spawn
    SURYA_INFERENCE_AUTOSTART: bool = True
    # Leave an auto-spawned server running after the process exits so later
    # commands attach to it instead of re-spawning (avoids repeated startup /
    # model-load cost). Stop it manually when done — see `surya/inference`.
    SURYA_INFERENCE_KEEP_ALIVE: bool = False

    SURYA_INFERENCE_PORT: Optional[int] = None  # None = pick a free port

    # Optional override for the *total* ctx passed to llama-server. When None

    SURYA_INFERENCE_CTX_SIZE: Optional[int] = None
    SURYA_INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: float = 600.0

    # Disabled: with no minItems in TABLE_REC_JSON_SCHEMA, the constrained

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""OCR with Occular-OCR (DBNet + SVTR + Russian n-gram beam LM).

Russian-first document OCR, ONNX Runtime on CPU. Raw verbatim output.

Usage:
  python occular_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out.txt> [n_pages]
"""
import glob
import os
import sys
import time

from occular import OCRPipeline, Settings

PAGES = sys.argv[1]
OUT = sys.argv[2]
N = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 63
DEVICE = os.environ.get("OCCULAR_DEVICE", "cpu")

pipe = OCRPipeline(Settings(gpu=(DEVICE == "cuda"), lm=True))

pages = sorted(
    p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(PAGES, "*"))
    if p.lower().endswith((".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"))
)[:N]
out = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8")
for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        lines = [ln.get("text", "") for ln in pipe.process_image(p) if ln.get("text")]
        txt = "\n".join(lines)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        txt = f"<ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}>"
    dt = time.time() - t0
    print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {os.path.basename(p)} {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
    out.write(f"===== {os.path.basename(p)} ({dt:.1f}s) =====\n{txt}\n\n")
    out.flush()
out.close()
print("[i] done", flush=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""OCR with RapidOCR (ONNX PP-OCRv5, East-Slavic recognizer).

RapidOCR is the ONNX-runtime port of PaddleOCR; this uses the same
`eslav_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec` weights as scripts/eslav_ocr.py but without
PaddlePaddle. Raw verbatim output.

Usage:
  python rapidocr_ocr.py <pages_dir> <out.txt> [n_pages]
"""
import glob
import os
import sys
import time

from rapidocr import LangRec, ModelType, OCRVersion, RapidOCR

PAGES = sys.argv[1]
OUT = sys.argv[2]
N = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 63
LANG = os.environ.get("RAPIDOCR_LANG", "eslav")

_params = {
    "Rec.lang_type": LangRec(LANG),
    "Rec.ocr_version": OCRVersion.PPOCRV5,
    "Rec.model_type": ModelType.MOBILE,
    "Det.ocr_version": OCRVersion.PPOCRV5,
    "Det.model_type": ModelType.MOBILE,
    "Global.log_level": "error",
}
engine = RapidOCR(params=_params)

pages = sorted(
    p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(PAGES, "*"))
    if p.lower().endswith((".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"))
)[:N]
out = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8")
for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        res = engine(p)
        txt = "\n".join(res.txts or ())
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        txt = f"<ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}>"
    dt = time.time() - t0
    print(f"[{i}/{len(pages)}] {os.path.basename(p)} {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
    out.write(f"===== {os.path.basename(p)} ({dt:.1f}s) =====\n{txt}\n\n")
    out.flush()
out.close()
print("[i] done", flush=True)
